topic: how does the TCP handshake work
narration: Before computers send data, they need to agree they're both ready and awake. But packets can get lost, duplicated, or arrive late. So how do they start safely?
description: Same dark background and same laptop left-mid and server right-mid nodes from hook for continuity, now zoomed out slightly. Center dotted muted=grey path connects them with slight wobble animation. Small rectangular data packets (fg=white) move along path. Red-tinted duplicate and out-of-order copies appear on cue. Large fg=white question text 'start safely?' fades in center-bottom of safe area at end. No elements in top 10% or bottom 25%.

beats.action: Camera pulls back revealing full dotted path between laptop and server nodes, both idle cyan and magenta.
White data packet forms above laptop and starts moving toward server along path.
Laptop and server nodes pulse awake with soft fg=white halos; READY checkmarks blink above each.
Path turns shaky wavy; three white packets in flight along dotted line.
Leading packet fades to transparent mid-flight and disappears.
Trailing packet splits into two overlapping red-tinted copies wobbling side by side.
A red packet arrives out of order jumping ahead, flashing red border to mark late arrival.
